title: AHA: Boehringer aims for 2027 survodutide submission after obesity drug passes cardio test
summary: Boehringer Ingelheim is gearing up to take survodutide to regulators next year after the obesity drug proved its cardiovascular credentials in its latest phase 3 study.

title: Spruce spins out preclinical endocrinology program into newly formed Adrenyx
summary: Spruce Biosciences is spinning out a preclinical endocrinology program into a newly formed subsidiary called Adrenyx Biosciences, supported with up to $50 million from an unnamed investor.

title: Zura scraps hidradenitis suppurativa program after phase 2 miss, sinking stock
summary: Zura Bio’s tibulizumab has flunked a phase 2 hidradenitis suppurativa trial, prompting the biotech to end development in the indication while continuing studies in other settings.

title: Sanofi-backed Windward breezes toward $204M IPO to fund respiratory pipeline from China
summary: Windward Bio is sailing toward the public markets with the aim of raising over $200 million in proceeds to fund two respiratory drugs licensed from China.

title: Advanced Analytics Help Reduce Control Animal Use While Preserving Scientific Rigor
summary: Advanced analytics leverage curated historical controls on new studies, supporting fewer animals while preserving scientific rigor.

title: Kyorin pens $140M deal for Japan rights to Edesa’s phase 3 respiratory drug
summary: Kyorin Pharmaceutical is paying $12 million upfront for the Japan rights to Edesa Biotech’s anti-TLR4 antibody to treat acute respiratory distress syndrome.

title: Faeth’s phase 2 data power oral combo forward in cancer targeted by ADC heavyweights
summary: Faeth Therapeutics’ endometrial cancer prospect has cleared the phase 2 efficacy bar, emboldening the biotech to forge ahead with efforts to establish the oral therapy in a field dominated by injectables.

title: Vir’s phase 3 hepatitis delta win fuels push to eclipse Gilead
summary: Vir Biotechnology’s phase 3 trial in chronic hepatitis delta has hit its primary endpoint, giving the biotech the first piece of the package it needs to file for FDA approval next year.

title: Valneva sees LimmaTech vaccine reduce Shigella infections in phase 2 test
summary: Valneva’s Shigella vaccine has been shown to reduce cases of intestinal infection, hitting the key endpoint of a phase 2 trial.

title: Argenx inks $1.15B Unnatural Products buyout to expand in oral peptides
summary: Argenx has struck a deal to acquire Unnatural Products for $550 million upfront, snapping up the Merck & Co.- and Novartis-partnered biotech to add oral peptide capabilities.

title: AHA: Novartis’ Lp(a) drug shows zero benefit, casting shadow over Amgen and Lilly programs
summary: Novartis has lifted the lid on data from its failed cardiovascular outcomes trial, reporting a total absence of efficacy that could intensify questions about upcoming readouts from Amgen and Eli Lilly.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Novo's longtime CFO to hang up gloves as Galderma exec steps in
summary: Novo's CFO of the past 8 years is taking his leave at the end of the year. Alnylam is on the hunt for a new commercial chief amid news of Tolga Tanguler's departure. Amgen has looked within to replace its head of quality.

title: There's more than one way to build a biotech
summary: Axiom Biosciences is taking an unconventional approach to raising capital and developing new therapies. In this episode of "The Top Line," founder and CEO Remo Moomiaie-Qajar joins Fierce Biotech's Marissa Russo to discuss the company's financing strategy, drug development approach and upcoming clinical milestones.

title: Generate CEO sees ‘huge opportunity’ from using Claude to shorten CAR-T cell engines
summary: Generate Biomedicines' CEO has hailed the “huge opportunity” offered by AI tools after the Flagship-founded company used Anthropic's Claude AI platform to reduce the size of CAR-T cell engines.

title: Moderna’s norovirus vaccine plans in limbo in wake of phase 3 miss
summary: Moderna has scrapped plans to enroll a new cohort in a phase 3 trial of its norovirus vaccine and instead will meet with regulators to decide on next steps.

title: Merck abandons Sutro-partnered IL-2 drug in ‘routine pipeline prioritization’
summary: Merck & Co. has called time on a Sutro Biopharma-partnered IL-2 agonist that was being tested for solid tumors.

title: Siemens Healthineers rebrands and carves out in vitro diagnostics biz
summary: Siemens Healthineers will carve out its in vitro diagnostics business as a standalone company operating under the name Olyrian Diagnostics.

title: Rezera revs up for $181M IPO to fund phase 3 trial of NLRP3 inhibitor
summary: Rezera—the new name for NodThera—is aiming for a $181 million IPO to take its NLRP3 inhibitor into phase 3 trials for a cardiovascular disease.

title: MetaVia sees GLP-1 shed liver fat and body weight in phase 1, takes aim at specific liver disease
summary: MetaVia has linked its GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist to reductions in liver fat and body weight in a phase 1 trial. Encouraged by the data, MetaVia plans to start a phase 2 trial in alcohol-associated liver disease next year.

title: AstraZeneca said to offer $10B to acquire Rhythm, analysts whisper of a bidding war
summary: AstraZeneca has made a roughly $10 billion offer to purchase rare obesity disease player Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, The Wall Street Journal reports. At least three teams of analysts suggest a bidding war could be brewing and that Rhythm is unlikely to settle for AZ’s current pitch.

title: Agios aims to shed over 100 R&D roles this year ahead of hoped-for sickle cell disease approval
summary: Agios Pharmaceuticals has been shrinking its R&D headcount over the course of 2026 as the commercial-stage company looks to eliminate more than 100 roles by year-end.

title: Cash-strapped Vivoryon regains China rights to kidney disease prospect from Simcere
summary: Vivoryon Therapeutics has regained the China rights to its kidney disease prospect as the German biotech’s cash reserves begin to dry up.

title: How “Pink Noise” in Conversation Makes Chats Enjoyable
summary: What makes a conversation truly click? Researchers discovered that enjoyable dialogues follow a mathematical rhythm called "pink noise", an organic ebb and flow of semantic alignment and divergence that predicts chemistry from speed dates to podcasts.

title: Can Obesity Drugs Protect the Brain?
summary: Can blockbuster weight-loss medications save your memory? A review in Science by researchers at the Universities of Copenhagen and Gothenburg dissects how GLP-1 drugs affect cognitive pathways, evaluating the boundary between systemic metabolic fixes and direct brain actions.

title: Estrogen Exposure Shields the Aging Brain
summary: Does lifetime estrogen protect the brain's microcirculation? A 5-year MRI study in Neurology reveals that a longer reproductive lifespan and hormone therapy use cut cerebral small vessel disease burden by up to 59%, preserving white matter integrity into older age.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, AAN, Aging, brain research, cerebral blood flow, cognition, estrogen, hormone replacement therapy, HRT, neurobiology

title: The Acoustic Science of What Makes a Great Singer
summary: What separates a good opera singer from a great one in the ears of competition judges? Keio University researchers simulated a live vocal competition, revealing that the 2–4 kHz "singer’s formant" and sex-specific vibrato tuning drive top marks, while raw loudness matters little.
category: Auditory Neuroscience, Featured, Neuroscience, acoustics, auditory neuroscience, brain research, Keio University, neurobiology, singers, vocalists

title: How Octopuses Lock in Long-Term Memory Without New Proteins
summary: How does an octopus hold onto memories without the molecular machinery used by humans? Researchers discovered a self-sustaining nitric oxide switch in the octopus vertical lobe that locks in long-term potentiation without requiring new protein synthesis.

title: Enriched Environments Rewire the Brain via Shared Synaptic Gene Networks
summary: How does an active, stimulating lifestyle physically rewire the brain? A meta-analysis of over 300 studies identifies a conserved molecular signature driven by the AP-1 transcription factor, unveiling the genomic machinery behind environmental enrichment.

title: Glioblastoma’s Chaos Follows Predictable Rules

title: One Autism Mutation Collapses the Whole Gene Network
summary: How can hundreds of different mutations cause autism? Boston Children's Hospital researchers discovered "transcriptomic convergence"—where mutating one autism gene drags down a whole network—and identified ZFX, an X-linked gene that protects females from the collapse.

title: Why Bitter Coffee Starts to Taste So Good to Your Brain
summary: Why do we learn to love the bitter taste of coffee? A study in Nature led by UCSF reveals an internal "slow" dopamine circuit connecting gut nutrient sensors to the left amygdala, building over minutes to link post-ingestive caloric rewards with new flavors.
